title: Sunshine and Storms: Weathering a Creative Life
note: Placeholder transcript for the AI Week demo, not a real transcription. Replace via generate_transcripts.py once ffmpeg + an OpenAI/Whisper key are available.

segments.text: Tad Carpenter opens by tracing the founding of Carpenter Collective, and why he frames a creative career as alternating 'sunshine and storms' rather than a steady upward line.
How the studio built its first award-winning brand identity system on a shoestring budget, and the specific client trust-building that made that first big win possible.
Weathering the 'storms' - a slow year with almost no new business, and the concrete changes to outreach and pricing that pulled the studio out of it.
Building a distinctive brand system: how Carpenter Collective develops a visual language (color, illustration, type) that stays consistent across packaging, signage, and digital.
Balancing the studio's own creative point of view against client asks - when to hold firm on a design decision and when a client's business context should override taste.
Growing from a solo freelancer into a small studio: hiring the first designer, and the specific mentoring habits that kept the studio's visual voice consistent as the team grew.
Maintaining creative energy over a long career - Tad's own routines (sketching outside of client work, side projects) that keep the work from feeling purely commercial.
Closing thoughts: treating both the wins and the slow periods as data about the business, not just morale swings, and using that to make steadier long-term decisions.
